original_idea.body:
# Code-of-Practice Vagueness x Selective Compliance: Measuring Where Soft Law Lets Big Labs Off Easy

**Problem:** EU GPAI Code of Practice uses vague language; compliance is uneven. Vagueness plus asymmetric capacity lets risky obligations be satisfied thinly.

**Direction:** Code each measure for linguistic hardness, map to observable compliance signals, compute a vagueness x observed-compliance grid.

**Why it matters:** Targets the gap between voluntary codes and enforceable standards. Public documents only.

**Relevant context:** dlapiper.com; artificialintelligenceact.eu; EU AI Office.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague impact: improving soft-law enforceability is broadly relevant but no specific catastrophic scenario or explicit chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Rubric-based policy-text coding with light NLP; novice+mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (the grid) with clear method, few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public-document analysis, squarely civil-society work outside labs.

novelty.reasoning: Soft-law analysis exists; this vagueness-x-compliance grid may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Policy-text hardness coding exists; the specific compliance-grid may be open.
